Web search results for query: "Supabase docs Row Level Security"

Links: [{"title":"Securing your API","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api"},{"title":"Securing your data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/secure-data"},{"title":"Database","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/overview"},{"title":"RAG with Permissions","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/rag-with-permissions"},{"title":"Tables and data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/tables"},{"title":"API keys","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys"},{"title":"Auth","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth"},{"title":"Production Checklist","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod"},{"title":"Supabase Docs","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting/storage-error-403-forbidden-new-row-violates-row-level-security-policy-on-upload-a94384"},{"title":"Realtime Authorization","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/authorization"}]

The search returned several Supabase docs pages on Row Level Security (RLS). The main one is the "Securing your API" guide, which covers how RLS combines with table grants for the Data API. The Tables and data page and the API keys page cover the practical setup and which roles policies apply to.

- **Setup:** The Tables and data page says that tables created in the Dashboard get RLS automatically, but tables created with SQL need it enabled manually. It also notes that until a policy exists, Data API requests return no rows. The Table Editor enables row level security for you when you create a table in the Dashboard. When you create a table with SQL, enable it yourself.
- **Grants vs. RLS:** The Securing your API guide separates the two layers. Grants decide whether a role can reach an object at all, and RLS decides which rows that role can see or change. Postgres evaluates table grants first, and only then applies Row Level Security.
- **Roles:** The API keys page explains which role each key maps to, which RLS policies match against. A publishable key without a signed-in user maps to the anon role, a publishable key with a signed-in user maps to authenticated, and a secret key maps to service_role. Policies never apply to a secret key, because service_role has the BYPASSRLS attribute.
- **Policy examples:** The Tables and data page shows an example of a per-user policy that compares the signed-in user's ID with a row's user_id column, and the Realtime Authorization page applies the same pattern to the realtime.messages table.
- **Common pitfall:** A Storage upload can fail with a 403 error if no SELECT policy covers the new object. The troubleshooting page explains that the database is unable to return the row metadata without that SELECT policy.

The main pages to read next are the Row Level Security guide itself and the Row Level Security Performance page, which is listed in the Database section.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.
